question.text: Chapter 2 gives an illustrative DIB proposition where an HNI donor may be pitched: 'a donation of INR 50,000 is to be paid only if two low-income/low-skilled youth are placed in jobs with incomes of over INR ______.' What is the income threshold?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 2.3.1.2 ('How DIBs can benefit from the SSE in India'), the illustrative proposition reads: 'a HNI donor may be pitched with a proposition that a donation of INR 50,000 is to be paid only if two low-income/ low-skilled youth are placed in jobs with incomes of over INR 15,000.' Cost-per-placement = Rs 25,000 per youth. The Trap: Options A, C and D are nearby distractors but not the chapter figure. Mis-remembering this detail produces wrong cost-per-outcome figures. Cross-Exam Context: X-A/X-B (IA) treats illustrative suitability examples for HNI clients. V-A (MF Distributor) similarly uses illustrative donation sizing. Assessor's Pro-Tip: For a livelihoods DIB, your SIR must specify the income-threshold definition (per month? per year? gross/net?) and sampling method — the illustrative INR 15,000 is likely monthly gross; ensure the NPO's measurement convention matches the donor's expectation to avoid disputes at outcome-payment time.
